summary: Discovery call for Ursa Systems evaluating Redwood's PLG/self-serve API with interest in quickstart, free credits, and options for hosted/dedicated/private. Customer cares about time-to-first-token, latency vs cost, and compliance (SOC2/KMS). AE+SE will run a demo and a small benchmark using a representative prompt set; next steps include sending quickstart materials and free credits.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Diego from our SE team. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] Raj Patel: Good, thanks Lena. Excited to learn more.
[00:10] Diego Martinez: Hey all - quick agenda, 1) understand your current stack & use case, 2) quick overview of Redwood PLG/quickstart, 3) discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private, and 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:22] Maya Chen: Yep sounds good. Just to flag, we have about 6 engineers who will try the quickstart, and we have a tight timeline - we'd like something up in a couple of weeks if possible.
[00:32] Omar Ali: Also security is a hard requirement - we need SOC2 and KMS integration, and potentially VPC/private option later.
[00:39] Lena Park: Totally understood. Can we start with the heavy lift - what are you trying to build and what does success look like?
[00:47] Raj Patel: We're building an internal assistant that surfaces infra runbooks and code snippets to our SREs. Latency is important for interactivity but cost is also a concern since we'll hit a few million tokens per month if it scales. Success = under 300ms median p99 for short prompts, and cost per 1k tokens under our current budget thresholds.
[01:05] Diego Martinez: Great, thanks. Are you evaluating open models or private models, and will this be a public cloud deployment?
[01:12] Maya Chen: We're fine with open models to start, maybe a small Llama-derived model for cost. We will probably start on hosted API to move fast and later consider dedicated or private for data isolation.
[01:22] Lena Park: That's the typical flow - PLG/self-serve hosted quickstart to get time-to-first-token then Dedicated when you need predictable throughput or Private for compliance. We offer free credits so engineers can spin up a test in under an hour.
[01:33] Raj Patel: Can you walk us through the quickstart? I'm less worried about the SDK and more about how fast my team can get a token and a latency reading.
[01:40] Diego Martinez: Sure - step one, sign up, you get API key and a small free credit bundle. Step two, sdk quickstart - e.g., a curl or python snippet to call text generation. In practice most teams run first request in 10-20 minutes; time-to-first-token often depends on network + model cold start.
[01:55] Maya Chen: You mentioned cold start - how variable is that? If we use a small open model on hosted, do you have warm pools?
[02:02] Lena Park: For hosted we maintain regional warm pools for popular models to keep cold starts low. For Dedicated you get reserved capacity and much lower variance; Private lets you control warm pools on your infra. There's a tradeoff vs cost.
[02:16] Raj Patel: On cost - do you do per-token billing on hosted? Any options for committed discounts?
[02:21] Lena Park: Hosted is usage-based per token and per embedding units. We can provide credits for pilots and your team can purchase committed reserved capacity for Dedicated later for discounts.
[02:31] Omar Ali: On the security front, can Redwood integrate with our KMS and provide audit logs for requests? We need to show this to compliance.
[02:38] Diego Martinez: Yes - Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs with configurable retention. Hosted has encrypted data at rest and in transit and RBAC/SAML SSO; SOC2 report available. For enterprise deals we can discuss longer log retention and audit export.
[02:55] Raj Patel: Are the hosted models multi-tenant? We need to be sure data isn't used for training.
[03:00] Lena Park: Hosted API by default does not use customer data for training. For extra guarantees, Dedicated or Private provides stronger isolation — Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools.
[03:09] Maya Chen: Could you explain where Dedicated sits operationally versus Private? We want to avoid managing Kubernetes ourselves if possible.
[03:15] Diego Martinez: Dedicated is managed by Redwood - we provision reserved GPUs in our fleet and you get guaranteed throughput; you don't manage infra. Private is customer-hosted control plane or on-prem package where you manage the infra (or partner-managed). Private is chosen when customers have strict network controls or air-gapped needs.
[03:31] Raj Patel: For our pilot, sounds like Hosted quickstart fits. We want to test a 7B-ish open model, measure latency & token quality, then decide whether to go Dedicated for production. Is that reasonable?
[03:39] Lena Park: Absolutely. Typical path is exactly that. We'll grant free credits and a quickstart guide. Diego can run a benchmark with your sample prompts, and we can show how batching, KV cache and quantization recommendations affect latency/cost.
[03:56] Omar Ali: You said KV cache - sometimes I see it written as K V cache in docs, just curious how disruption works.
[04:02] Diego Martinez: Ha, yes transcriptionism. KV cache is basically the key-value cache used to speed up autoregressive decoding for long conversations. Redwood does prefix caching and can cache embeddings as well to reduce per-token work. That typically helps latency for interactive sessions.
[04:17] Raj Patel: For the benchmark, what metrics will you provide? We want median latency, p95, p99, cost per 1k tokens and memory footprint.
[04:25] Diego Martinez: We'll provide median/p95/p99 latencies, per-token cost estimate, request concurrency and throughput, and a recommended deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated/private) with expected unit economics. We'll also attach a spreadsheet so you can tweak batch sizes and see cost tradeoffs.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Do you support streaming and tool calling? We plan to stream partial answers into our UI.
[04:45] Lena Park: Yes, hosted supports streaming, function/tool calling and structured output. That tends to help perceived latency in UIs.
[04:52] Raj Patel: Any gotchas on data residency? Some of our logs must stay in EU region only.
[04:57] Diego Martinez: We can provision regional endpoints; hosted has EU regions and data residency options. For strict residency you might consider Dedicated or Private.
[05:06] Omar Ali: On the free credits - what's the size? Enough to run a small benchmark?
[05:10] Lena Park: We typically grant $1,000 of credits for pilots which is more than enough for a week of benchmarking at small scale. We'll include that in the email.
[05:18] Raj Patel: Great. Timeline - we want pilot ready in ~2 weeks. Is Redwood able to support that?
[05:23] Lena Park: Yes, provided we get your prompt set and sample inputs. Diego: can you schedule the technical demo this week?
[05:28] Diego Martinez: Yep I'll send available slots. Also I'll ask for schema of prompts and expected concurrency so we can simulate load.
[05:35] Maya Chen: Will the quickstart require any special infra access?
[05:38] Lena Park: No, for hosted quickstart you just need network access to the public API endpoint and an API key. For Dedicated/Private we can talk about networking once we scope it.
[05:47] Raj Patel: Any limitations on model variants exposed through the quickstart?
[05:51] Diego Martinez: Most curated open models are available; some custom quantized variants we reserve for Dedicated due to compatibility, but for 7B open models you should be fine on hosted.
[06:00] Omar Ali: Can we get a short security deck or SOC2 report to review with our compliance team?
[06:04] Lena Park: Yes - I'll attach our security pack and SOC2 summary in the follow-up.
[06:09] Raj Patel: Perfect. Also, we may reach out to your billing team about committed usage options if the pilot looks good.
[06:15] Lena Park: Absolutely.
[06:18] Diego Martinez: Ok quick recap: we'll send quickstart guide + free credits link, Diego will schedule a technical demo and prepare benchmark spreadsheet, Ursa to share prompt set & infra diagram, and we'll align on pilot timeline for Q2.
[06:31] Raj Patel: That sounds great. Thanks everyone.
[06:34] Lena Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials.
[06:38] Maya Chen: Appreciate it.
[06:40] Omar Ali: Thanks.
[06:42] [END]
